risks.quote: Providers shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system in a manner that is proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and the risks of the high-risk AI system.
risks.engineering_action: If the system is classified as high-risk, add a post-market monitoring plan covering the highlighting function. It should track false negatives and false positives of highlights, using user reports (FR-14.2) and caregiver feedback, and define thresholds that trigger corrective action. Document the plan in the technical documentation.

recommendations: If the system is classified as high-risk, establish and document a post-market monitoring plan that measures the accuracy of FR-13.5 highlights (missed and false alerts) and defines corrective-action triggers.

requirement_text: The system shall allow users to provide feedback about app usability and AI responses.

assessment.summary: FR-14.1 is a simple user feedback feature. The supplied provisions (AI Office powers, sandboxes, notified bodies, Commission reviews) impose no obligation on this requirement. The only loosely relevant provisions, Article 4 (AI literacy) and Article 50 (transparency), are already addressed elsewhere in the SRS.

requirement_text: The system shall allow users to report incorrect or unsafe AI advice.

assessment.summary: FR-14.2 gives users a way to report incorrect or unsafe AI advice, but nothing says what happens to those reports: no triage, no investigation, no escalation to serious-incident or corrective-action processes. Without that, reports could go unactioned and the provider could miss its duties to investigate, correct and notify authorities.

risks.description: User reports of unsafe AI advice are not tied to a process that assesses whether they indicate non-conformity or a risk, so investigation and corrective action are not triggered.
risks.quote: shall immediately take the necessary corrective actions to bring that system into conformity, to withdraw it, to disable it, or to recall it, as appropriate.
risks.engineering_action: Route reports into a triage workflow with severity classification, an owner, an investigation SLA, and a documented path to corrective action (fix, disable feature, rollback) and to informing deployers and distributors.

addressed_by.covers: correct or remove inaccurate recommendations once identified (corrective action)

risks.description: Reports of harmful advice are not classified against the serious-incident criteria, so reportable incidents could go unnotified to market surveillance authorities and no incident investigation or risk assessment is triggered.
risks.quote: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred.
risks.engineering_action: Add a serious-incident screening step to report handling (e.g. harm to health, death) with escalation to the compliance owner, authority notification within the deadlines, and preservation of the AI system state and logs for investigation (Art. 73(6)).

addressed_by.covers: logging of AI-generated advice that can support incident investigation

risks.description: The requirement does not specify that reports capture enough context (the AI output, inputs, version) or feed monitoring of anomalies and unexpected performance, which limits the ability to detect and address errors and faults.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be as resilient as possible regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies that may occur within the system or the environment in which the system operates, in particular due to their interaction with natural persons or other systems.
risks.engineering_action: Link each report to the logged AI response, model version and context; aggregate reports into error metrics reviewed regularly, and feed confirmed errors into testing and the knowledge base while guarding against feedback loops.

addressed_by.covers: AI advice logs for audit and safety review

recommendations: Define a triage and corrective-action workflow for user reports, with owners, SLAs and escalation to deployers/distributors.
Add serious-incident screening and authority notification to report handling, preserving evidence for investigation.
Capture AI output, version and context with each report and feed aggregated reports into accuracy monitoring and regression testing.

requirement_text: The system shall allow users to confirm whether they have taken, skipped, or delayed a medication.

assessment.summary: FR-2.3 is a basic user input function (confirming a medication as taken, skipped, or delayed). None of the supplied provisions, which cover notified bodies, certificates, market surveillance procedures, GPAI systemic risk, sandboxes and Annex III amendments, impose a requirement-level obligation on it.

requirement_text: The system shall provide an AI-powered virtual assistant that can answer general health-related questions in simple language.

assessment.summary: FR-3.1 is a conversational health assistant that interacts directly with natural persons, so Article 50(1) requires users to be told they are talking to an AI. Nothing in FR-3.1 or the other requirements clearly states that disclosure at the point of interaction. The requirement also does not address machine-readable marking of generated text.

risks.description: FR-3.1 does not require that users are informed at the point of interaction that they are talking to an AI system. Older adults may not find this obvious, and FR-11.5, NFR-12.3 and NFR-15.3 only label recommendations or advice, not the chat interaction itself.
risks.quote: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system
risks.engineering_action: Add to FR-3.1 that the assistant discloses its AI nature at the start of every chat or voice session, in plain language and in audio for voice interaction.

addressed_by.covers: indicates when recommendations are AI-generated (labelling of outputs, not disclosure of the interaction)
identifies whether advice came from AI, a caregiver, or a healthcare professional

risks.description: The assistant generates synthetic text, but no requirement says that outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and are detectable as AI-generated.
risks.quote: shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated
risks.engineering_action: Add machine-readable provenance metadata to assistant outputs, such as exported chat transcripts and reports, or document why the obligation does not apply.

recommendations: Specify in FR-3.1 a clear AI-interaction disclosure at the start of each text or voice session.
Add machine-readable marking of generated text outputs, or record the rationale for any exemption.

requirement_text: The system shall provide health guidance based on the user’s profile, symptoms, and history where appropriate.

assessment.summary: FR-3.3 makes the system produce personalised health guidance from profile, symptoms and history without defining the guidance scope, its accuracy or the risks it carries. No risk analysis for this function, and no data-quality or bias controls for the profile and history data behind it, are specified. Neither the high-risk classification nor the Article 6(3) exemption is documented. The system's own AI-labelling, logging, clinical-review and bias-review requirements cover only part of this.

risks.description: Personalised guidance for older adults from health history and symptoms has no risk management process identifying and mitigating foreseeable risks (unsafe advice, vulnerable-group harm). Existing safety requirements are generic and not tied to a lifecycle risk process for this function.
risks.quote: the identification and analysis of the known and the reasonably foreseeable risks that the high-risk AI system can pose to health, safety or fundamental rights when the high-risk AI system is used in accordance with its intended purpose
risks.engineering_action: Define a documented, iterative risk management process covering the guidance function, including misuse, with targeted mitigations and post-market feedback loops.

addressed_by.covers: mitigation measure against unsafe, overconfident or unsupported recommendations (9(2)(d))
channel for reports of unsafe advice, usable as post-market data input (9(2)(c))

risks.description: The requirement does not consider that the users are older adults, a potentially vulnerable group, when guidance is generated.
risks.quote: providers shall give consideration to whether in view of its intended purpose the high-risk AI system is likely to have an adverse impact on persons under the age of 18 and, as appropriate, other vulnerable groups.
risks.engineering_action: Add an explicit assessment of adverse impacts on older and cognitively impaired users, with acceptance criteria and mitigations for guidance outputs.

addressed_by.covers: avoiding ageist assumptions in recommendations (design consideration for a vulnerable group)

risks.description: Profile, symptom and history data drive the guidance, but no data governance is specified for their quality, representativeness or bias. NFR-12.7 only reviews bias in outputs, with no mitigation or data-set criteria.
risks.quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
risks.engineering_action: Specify data governance for training, validation and testing data used in personalisation: representativeness across age, gender and conditions, bias examination, and mitigation measures with thresholds.

addressed_by.covers: process for reviewing bias in AI recommendations (examination for bias, 10(2)(f))

risks.description: Instructions for use for deployers (clinicians and caregivers) must state intended purpose, accuracy metrics and limitations. FR-3.3 uses 'where appropriate' without defining the intended purpose or performance bounds of the guidance.
risks.quote: the characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance of the high-risk AI system, including: (i) its intended purpose; (ii) the level of accuracy, including its metrics
risks.engineering_action: Define the intended purpose and scope of the guidance (what 'where appropriate' means), declare accuracy metrics and known limitations, and include them in the instructions for use.

addressed_by.covers: confidence or uncertainty indicators for outputs (13(3)(b)(vii) interpretation of output)

risks.description: Human oversight of the personalised guidance is not defined in this requirement; clinical review is limited to 'high-risk AI outputs' with no criteria for which guidance triggers it.
risks.quote: they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use
risks.engineering_action: Define which guidance outputs trigger clinical review and how overseers can interpret, override or stop them.

addressed_by.covers: clinical review of high-risk AI outputs
user ability to challenge, correct or dismiss AI suggestions

recommendations: Establish a lifecycle risk management process for the guidance function with documented mitigations and post-market inputs.
Add an explicit assessment of risks to older and vulnerable users, with acceptance criteria.
Define data governance and bias mitigation for profile, symptom and history data, with thresholds.
Define the intended purpose, scope and accuracy metrics for guidance, and publish them in the instructions for use.
Define criteria that trigger clinical review and oversight of guidance outputs.

requirement_text: The system shall allow users to record symptoms such as pain, dizziness, shortness of breath, fatigue, fever, or confusion.

assessment.summary: FR-4.1 is a plain symptom-entry function and sits upstream of the AI triage in FR-4.3/4.4. It adds no direct AI Act gap of its own; the only point is that these inputs feed the AI function and should be covered by logging and data governance. Whether the system is high-risk is not settled by this requirement.

risks.description: Recorded symptom entries feed the AI urgency classification (FR-4.3) and recommendations (FR-4.4). Logging of AI advice exists (NFR-3.6), but it is not specified to include the symptom input events and the period of use. This weakens traceability if the system is high-risk.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for:
risks.engineering_action: Extend the NFR-3.6 logging scope so that symptom inputs (timestamped, linked to the resulting urgency classification and recommendation) are retained as events, with retention aligned to NFR-13.3.

addressed_by.covers: automatic logging of AI-generated advice for auditing and safety review

recommendations: Make sure symptom input events are included in the audit/event logging that supports the AI triage outputs (extend NFR-3.6 to cover inputs).

requirement_text: The system shall ask follow-up questions to better understand reported symptoms.

assessment.summary: FR-4.2 only covers collecting more symptom detail through follow-up questions. None of the supplied provisions (serious incident reporting, post-market monitoring, notified-body and GPAI procedures) impose an obligation on this requirement's own wording. Incident reporting and post-market monitoring are system-level processes that belong to the SRS as a whole, not to this requirement.

requirement_text: The system shall allow users to store appointment details such as doctor name, clinic location, reason for visit, and preparation notes.

assessment.summary: FR-6.3 is a plain data-storage function for appointment details (doctor, clinic, reason, notes) with no AI decision-making. None of the supplied provisions impose a requirement-level obligation on it, so no compliance gap is identified.

requirement_text: The system shall provide a clearly visible emergency assistance button.

assessment.summary: FR-7.1 is a UI requirement for an emergency assistance button, a user-facing safety control. The supplied provisions do not support a requirement-level gap for it. Arts. 28, 90, 70, 52, 31, 82, 21 and 7 address authorities, notified bodies or the Commission, not this requirement. Art. 14(4)(e) 'stop' button concerns halting the AI system, which is not what an emergency call button does. Art. 73 reporting is a system-level process, not an obligation on this button.

requirement_text: The system shall allow caregivers to send reminders or supportive messages to the older adult.

assessment.summary: FR-8.4 is a caregiver-to-older-adult messaging feature. The supplied provisions (Articles 28-45) cover notifying authorities and notified bodies, not providers or deployers of AI systems, so they impose no requirement-level obligation on this requirement.

requirement_text: The system shall maintain an activity log of caregiver actions for transparency.

assessment.summary: FR-8.6 logs only caregiver actions, so it is not a substitute for the automatic, lifetime event logging of the AI system's own operation that Article 12 requires if the system is high-risk. It also sets no minimum retention period, which would weaken traceability and authority access to logs. This is engineering review support, not legal advice, and it assumes the system is classed as high-risk.

risks.description: The log is scoped to caregiver actions for 'transparency', not to automatic recording of system events relevant to identifying risk situations or substantial modifications, post-market monitoring, and deployer operational monitoring.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for:
risks.engineering_action: Define a system-level event logging specification covering AI outputs, urgency classifications, model and version changes, overrides, user challenges and errors. Tie each event type to Art. 12(2)(a)-(c) purposes, and keep caregiver-action logging as one source within it.

addressed_by.covers: automatic recording of AI-generated advice for auditing and safety review (partial: AI output events only)
audit logs of access to sensitive information (partial: access events)

risks.description: No retention period is set for the caregiver activity log; the generic retention policy requirement does not fix the minimum of at least six months.
risks.quote: the logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
risks.engineering_action: Add a retention rule to FR-8.6 of at least six months, or longer if justified by purpose. Reconcile it with data-protection deletion rights (NFR-13.5, NFR-4.3), and make the logs tamper-evident and available to competent authorities on reasoned request.

addressed_by.covers: data retention and deletion policies in general (no minimum period for logs)

recommendations: Create a system-wide event logging specification aligned with Art. 12(2) and covering AI behaviour, model changes and risk-relevant events, not only caregiver actions.
Specify log retention of at least six months in FR-8.6, reconcile it with deletion rights, and make the logs tamper-evident and retrievable for authorities.

requirement_text: The app shall use a simple and intuitive interface suitable for older adults.

assessment.summary: NFR-1.1 is a general usability statement that supports accessibility and does not raise a substantive AI Act gap by itself. The only relevant provision is Art. 50(5), which requires AI-interaction disclosures to be clear and accessible. Other requirements already cover that.

requirement_text: The app shall support guided onboarding for first-time users.

assessment.summary: The onboarding requirement has little direct AI Act exposure. The one remaining point is that it does not say onboarding should tell first-time users they are interacting with an AI system. Other requirements label AI output but do not fix the timing at first interaction.

risks.description: Onboarding does not state that it discloses AI interaction (assistant, symptom triage, recommendations) before or at the user's first interaction, in an accessible form. Existing requirements label AI output only after it is produced.
risks.quote: The information referred to in paragraphs 1 to 4 shall be provided to the natural persons concerned in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure.
risks.engineering_action: Add an onboarding step, before first use of the AI assistant or recommendations, that states the app uses AI and what it does. Make the step conform to accessibility requirements (large text, audio, screen reader).

addressed_by.covers: indicates when recommendations are AI-generated (50(1) disclosure, per output)
identifies whether advice came from AI, a caregiver, or a professional

recommendations: Extend NFR-1.6 so guided onboarding includes an accessible AI-interaction disclosure shown no later than the first interaction with the AI assistant or AI-generated recommendations.

requirement_text: The system shall support an increasing number of users without major performance degradation.

assessment.summary: NFR-10.1 is a generic scalability requirement. The supplied provisions do not support a requirement-level compliance gap; Art. 15(4) resilience is only loosely related and is covered by NFR-14.x and NFR-6.x.

requirement_text: The system shall support scaling of AI services during peak usage.

assessment.summary: NFR-10.2 is a generic scalability requirement. The listed provisions impose no obligation on peak-load scaling, and the one nearby provision (Art. 15(4) resilience) is already covered by other availability and recovery requirements.

requirement_text: The app shall support integration with common wearable devices and health monitoring tools.

assessment.summary: NFR-11.1 is a vague integration statement. It sets no device scope, data provenance or data-suitability expectations for wearable inputs that feed health-pattern AI features. Unvetted sensor data could weaken the AI features' reliability and introduce bias for older users.

risks.description: No requirement defines which wearable and monitoring devices are supported, how their data origin is recorded, or how sensor data is checked for quality and suitability before AI use (including any reuse for model improvement).
risks.quote: data collection processes and the origin of data, and in the case of personal data, the original purpose of the data collection;
risks.engineering_action: Name the supported device classes and standards. Record device and source metadata with each reading. Add data-quality checks (range, missing data, calibration) and document how wearable data is prepared and used for AI features and model improvement.

risks.description: Wearable sensor accuracy varies by device, skin tone, motion and the health conditions of older adults. Nothing requires data sets to reflect this setting or requires an examination for resulting bias.
risks.quote: Data sets shall take into account, to the extent required by the intended purpose, the characteristics or elements that are particular to the specific geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional setting within which the high-risk AI system is intended to be used.
risks.engineering_action: Validate integrated devices against older-adult and demographically diverse populations. Document known accuracy limits per device. Include device-related bias checks in the bias review process (NFR-12.7).

addressed_by.covers: a process for reviewing bias in AI recommendations, which could be extended to device-related data bias (10(2)(f))

recommendations: Specify supported devices and add provenance metadata and data-quality validation for wearable inputs.
Validate device data accuracy for the older-adult setting and add device-related bias examination to the existing bias review process.

requirement_text: The app shall respect user autonomy and allow older adults to make their own decisions where possible.

assessment.summary: NFR-12.2 states a general autonomy principle but names no oversight capability, so it does not show that the system can be effectively overseen by natural persons. Concrete controls already exist elsewhere in the SRS (NFR-15.4, NFR-8.6, FR-14.5), leaving only a low-severity gap in how this requirement is worded and linked to them.

risks.description: The autonomy statement is vague ('where possible') and has no testable oversight mechanism, such as the ability to override, ignore or reverse AI outputs and recommendations. It also does not set criteria for when the user keeps the decision and when it is escalated, such as in emergencies or with cognitively impaired users.
risks.quote: The oversight measures shall be commensurate with the risks, level of autonomy and context of use of the high-risk AI system
risks.engineering_action: Reword NFR-12.2 into testable criteria. Require that every AI recommendation can be declined or overridden without penalty, that no AI-driven action is taken without user confirmation except in defined emergencies, and that the requirement traces to NFR-15.4, NFR-8.6 and FR-14.5. Add handling for caregiver-assisted or cognitively impaired users so that autonomy is preserved and oversight is not delegated by default.

addressed_by.covers: lets users challenge, correct or dismiss AI-generated suggestions, which is the override and disregard capability in the human-machine interface (14(1), 14(4)(d))
clinical review of high-risk AI outputs by natural persons
lets users request human assistance, which supports human intervention

recommendations: Rewrite NFR-12.2 with measurable acceptance criteria. Require user override or dismissal of all AI suggestions, confirmation before AI-driven actions, and defined emergency exceptions, and trace it to NFR-15.4, NFR-8.6 and FR-14.5.

requirement_text: The app shall clearly distinguish between AI advice and human clinical advice.

assessment.summary: NFR-12.3 requires the app to distinguish AI advice from human clinical advice, which broadly supports transparency. However, it does not specify that users are told they are interacting with an AI system, nor how the distinction is delivered (UI labelling, voice channel).

risks.description: The requirement does not state that users are informed they are interacting with an AI system (the virtual assistant via text and voice). 'Clearly distinguish' advice does not clearly cover disclosure at the point of interaction, including the voice channel and older or cognitively impaired users.
risks.quote: the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system
risks.engineering_action: Reword the requirement to specify the mechanism: persistent AI labelling in text and voice interactions, with disclosure at session start, tested for older adults and users with cognitive impairment. Include a measurable acceptance criterion.

addressed_by.covers: identifies whether advice came from AI, a caregiver, or a healthcare professional (labelling of advice source)
clearly indicates when recommendations are AI-generated

recommendations: Make NFR-12.3 testable by specifying persistent AI labelling in text and voice, with disclosure at session start, and cross-reference NFR-15.3 and FR-11.5 to avoid duplicate or inconsistent labelling.

requirement_text: The app shall be designed to support independence, not replace human care.

assessment.summary: NFR-12.5 is a high-level design principle (support independence, do not replace human care). The supplied provisions impose no binding obligation on this wording, and the related human-oversight, transparency and escalation controls already exist in other requirements (NFR-15.4, NFR-8.6, FR-14.5, NFR-3.2).

requirement_text: The app shall maintain records needed for clinical safety audits.

assessment.summary: NFR-13.3 requires 'records needed for clinical safety audits' but does not define which events are logged, the retention period, or the link to post-market monitoring. Without that, the logs may not give the traceability Article 12 requires or be kept as Article 19 requires.

risks.description: The requirement does not specify automatic recording of events over the system lifetime that enable traceability, such as identifying risk situations, supporting post-market monitoring and operational monitoring. 'Records needed for audits' is vague, and NFR-3.6 logs only AI advice.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for:
risks.engineering_action: Define the event types to log automatically: AI outputs and urgency classifications, clinician overrides, user reports of unsafe advice, model updates, and emergency escalations. Map each to Article 12(2)(a)-(c).

addressed_by.covers: automatic logging of AI-generated advice for auditing and safety review (partial traceability of system functioning)

risks.description: No retention period is stated for the audit records or logs. Article 19 requires logs under the provider's control to be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, and at least six months. NFR-13.5 covers generic retention and deletion but sets no minimum for safety logs.
risks.quote: the logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
risks.engineering_action: State a retention period of at least six months for safety audit logs, and exempt them from user-initiated deletion where law allows. Reconcile this with the data protection rules in NFR-13.1 and NFR-13.5.

addressed_by.covers: data retention and deletion policy mechanism (does not set a log retention period)

recommendations: Specify the automatically logged event categories and map them to Article 12(2)(a)-(c).
Set a minimum log retention period of at least six months and reconcile it with deletion rights.

requirement_text: The system shall maintain regular backups of user data.

assessment.summary: NFR-14.1 is a generic user-data backup requirement; none of the supplied provisions impose a requirement-level obligation on backups of user data. Log retention (Art. 12/19/26) concerns AI-generated logs, which this requirement does not address, and NFR-3.6 and NFR-5.5 already cover logging.

requirement_text: The system shall support disaster recovery procedures.

assessment.summary: NFR-14.2 only says disaster recovery procedures are "supported". It sets no recovery objectives, scope, or testing, and does not state that AI components, logs and safety functions are restored. Without these, the robustness and fail-safe expectations in Art. 15(4) are only partly met.

risks.description: The disaster recovery requirement has no measurable recovery objectives (RTO/RPO), no scope covering AI models, safety-critical functions (urgency classification, emergency escalation) or restoration to a known-safe state, and no testing, so it does not show resilience to faults as Art. 15(4) requires.
risks.quote: The robustness of high-risk AI systems may be achieved through technical redundancy solutions, which may include backup or fail-safe plans.
risks.engineering_action: Rewrite the requirement to define RTO/RPO per component. Include AI models and configuration, and the safety-critical emergency and escalation functions. Require restoration to a validated safe state and periodic DR drills with documented results.

addressed_by.covers: regular backups of user data (backup element of technical redundancy)
emergency information remains accessible during service disruption (fail-safe behaviour)
graceful recovery from system errors

risks.description: The requirement does not say that event logs (AI advice logs, access audit logs) are covered by backup and recovery, so traceability records could be lost in a disaster.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.
risks.engineering_action: State that DR procedures preserve and restore AI advice logs and audit logs, keeping their integrity and retention, and check this in DR tests.

addressed_by.covers: logging of AI-generated advice for auditing
audit logs for access to sensitive information

recommendations: Define RTO/RPO, scope (AI models, safety functions) and a safe-state restore, and schedule DR testing.
Include AI advice and audit logs in backup and DR scope, and verify their integrity after restore.

requirement_text: The system shall notify users of planned maintenance where possible.

assessment.summary: NFR-14.4 is an operational availability requirement (planned maintenance notices). The supplied provisions (Arts. 28, 30, 31, 34, 36, 37, 45, 27(3)) concern notifying authorities and notified bodies, or deployer notification to market surveillance authorities. None imposes an obligation on user maintenance notices, so no requirement-level gap is identified.

requirement_text: The app shall explain why important alerts or recommendations were generated.

assessment.summary: NFR-15.1 requires explanations for alerts and recommendations but does not say who the explanations are for or what they contain. It also does not tie them to the output interpretation that oversight persons need. Several related requirements (FR-3.6, NFR-12.6, NFR-8.4) already cover part of this, so the remaining gap is mainly about specifying the content and audience.

risks.description: The explanation requirement is vague about audience and content (inputs, logic, confidence, limitations). The people assigned oversight (caregivers, clinicians) therefore may not be enabled to correctly interpret the alert and recommendation outputs of the urgency-classification, emergency-detection and anomaly-detection functions.
risks.quote: to correctly interpret the high-risk AI system’s output, taking into account, for example, the interpretation tools and methods available;
risks.engineering_action: Specify the explanation content per alert type (key contributing inputs, urgency rationale, confidence, limitations). Provide a version for clinicians and caregivers as well as for older adults. Define which alerts count as 'important' (e.g. FR-4.3 urgency, FR-7.5 emergency, FR-10.5 wellbeing, FR-4.6 anomalies).

addressed_by.covers: plain-language explanation of AI-generated suggestions (assistant only)
confidence or uncertainty indicators supporting output interpretation
clinical review of high-risk AI outputs

risks.description: The requirement does not oblige the system to supply deployers with documented information on how outputs are generated and how to interpret them. The instructions for use are not addressed, and 'important' is undefined.
risks.quote: include concise, complete, correct and clear information that is relevant, accessible and comprehensible to deployers.
risks.engineering_action: Add to the instructions for use and documentation a description of the explanation mechanism, its limits, and how deployers (clinicians, caregivers) should interpret it. Check the explanations against NFR-12.6 and NFR-9.4 for consistency.

addressed_by.covers: documentation for developers and administrators

recommendations: Define the content, audience and trigger scope of alert and recommendation explanations, and align them with FR-3.6, NFR-8.4 and NFR-12.6.
Document the explanation mechanism and its limitations in the instructions for use provided to deployers.

requirement_text: The app shall avoid creating false reassurance when symptoms may require medical attention.

assessment.summary: None of the supplied provisions (notified body procedures, GPAI systemic-risk notification, importer/distributor duties, etc.) imposes an obligation on this requirement's function of avoiding false reassurance in symptom guidance. No requirement-level gap can be supported from the listed provisions.

requirement_text: The app shall comply with recognised accessibility guidelines such as WCAG 2.2 where applicable.

assessment.summary: NFR-2.1 commits to WCAG 2.2 'where applicable' but is vague and does not tie accessibility to the AI Act's accessibility duty for high-risk systems (Directives 2016/2102 and 2019/882) or to the accessibility of Article 50 transparency information. Detailed accessibility features exist in NFR-2.2 to NFR-2.8 and FR-1.6, so only the compliance anchoring and evidence gaps remain.

risks.description: The requirement cites only 'such as WCAG 2.2 where applicable' and does not name Directives (EU) 2016/2102 and (EU) 2019/882 or a conformance level (e.g. AA), so conformity with the accessibility obligation for a likely high-risk health AI system cannot be demonstrated.
risks.quote: ensure that the high-risk AI system complies with accessibility requirements in accordance with Directives (EU) 2016/2102 and (EU) 2019/882.
risks.engineering_action: Reword NFR-2.1 to require conformance at a defined WCAG 2.2 level (e.g. AA) and compliance with Directives 2016/2102 and 2019/882. Remove the 'where applicable' escape and keep an accessibility conformance report and test evidence in the technical documentation.

addressed_by.covers: screen reader support as one accessibility feature
high contrast display options as one accessibility feature
support for users with reduced vision, hearing, dexterity or cognitive ability

risks.description: Nothing states that AI-disclosure and transparency notices (AI-generated labels, AI vs human advice) must meet the accessibility requirements, so these notices could be inaccessible to older adults with disabilities.
risks.quote: The information shall conform to the applicable accessibility requirements.
risks.engineering_action: Add an acceptance criterion that AI-interaction disclosures, AI-generated content labels and disclaimers are delivered in accessible forms (screen reader, audio, high contrast) at first interaction, and test them against WCAG 2.2.

addressed_by.covers: indicating when recommendations are AI-generated (the disclosure itself, not its accessibility)

recommendations: Make NFR-2.1 a binding conformance target (WCAG 2.2 AA plus Directives 2016/2102 and 2019/882) and document the test evidence.
Extend accessibility acceptance criteria to AI transparency notices and disclaimers, and verify them with assistive-technology testing.

requirement_text: The app shall allow users to slow down or repeat voice instructions.

assessment.summary: NFR-2.8 is an accessibility control that lets users slow down or repeat voice instructions. None of the supplied provisions imposes a requirement-level gap on it. Art. 50(5) accessibility applies to AI-disclosure information, and that is covered by other requirements.

requirement_text: The app shall escalate potentially serious symptoms to emergency or professional care guidance.

assessment.summary: NFR-3.2 escalates serious symptoms to emergency guidance but defines no criteria, accuracy targets or failure analysis for missed escalations. A missed escalation could cause serious harm to health. Nothing in the SRS links such failures to serious-incident detection or reporting.

risks.description: The escalation function has no identified or evaluated risk of false negatives (missed urgent symptoms) or wrong escalation, and no defined risk management measures or acceptance thresholds.
risks.quote: the identification and analysis of the known and the reasonably foreseeable risks that the high-risk AI system can pose to health, safety or fundamental rights
risks.engineering_action: Add a risk analysis for the escalation function covering missed or delayed escalation and misclassification. Set sensitivity targets for urgent and emergency symptoms, test them, and record the residual risk and mitigations.

addressed_by.covers: emergency instructions once urgent symptoms are detected (a risk mitigation measure under 9(2)(d))

risks.description: No process detects, escalates or reports serious incidents (e.g. a missed emergency leading to death or serious harm) to market surveillance authorities within the Article 73 deadlines.
risks.quote: The report referred to in paragraph 1 shall be made immediately after the provider has established a causal link between the AI system and the serious incident or the reasonable likelihood of such a link, and, in any event, not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, becomes aware of the serious incident.
risks.engineering_action: Define a serious-incident workflow. It should triage reports of failed or missed escalation (including those from FR-14.2) against Article 3(49), set the 15-day, 10-day and 2-day reporting clocks, and cover investigation and preservation of the system state.

addressed_by.covers: user reports of unsafe AI advice, as an intake channel for incidents
logging of AI advice, which supports investigation of an incident

recommendations: Add a documented risk analysis for the escalation function, with measurable sensitivity targets for urgent and emergency symptoms and test evidence.
Establish a serious-incident detection and reporting procedure that triages missed or failed escalations against Article 3(49) and tracks the Article 73 deadlines.

requirement_text: The app shall include safeguards against hallucinated medical advice.

assessment.summary: NFR-3.4 names no concrete hallucination safeguard, no measurable acceptance criterion and no oversight trigger, so it cannot show that risks to health from false medical advice are minimised. Hallucination rates and known limitations are also not required to be documented for deployers.

risks.description: The requirement says 'safeguards' without specifying built-in measures (for example grounding checks, output blocking or escalation, or HMI cues). It also gives no acceptance criteria, so oversight cannot be shown to be commensurate with the health risk of fabricated medical advice.
risks.quote: measures identified and built, when technically feasible, into the high-risk AI system by the provider before it is placed on the market or put into service;
risks.engineering_action: Rewrite NFR-3.4 to name the safeguards: for example grounding to approved sources, a refusal or fallback when the answer is unsupported, and routing of high-risk outputs to clinical review. Add a testable acceptance criterion such as a maximum hallucination rate on a medical test set.

addressed_by.covers: clinical review of high-risk AI outputs as a human oversight measure
user ability to challenge, correct or dismiss AI suggestions
channel for users to report incorrect or unsafe AI advice

risks.description: Nothing in the SRS requires hallucination or factual-accuracy metrics, or the known failure circumstances, to be tested and documented in the instructions for use. Deployers such as clinicians and caregivers therefore cannot judge how far to rely on the advice.
risks.quote: the level of accuracy, including its metrics, robustness and cybersecurity referred to in Article 15 against which the high-risk AI system has been tested and validated and which can be expected, and any known and foreseeable circumstances that may have an impact on that expected level of accuracy
risks.engineering_action: Define hallucination and accuracy metrics, run validation against them, and record the results and known failure modes (for example rare conditions or ambiguous symptoms) in the instructions for use.

recommendations: Specify concrete, testable anti-hallucination safeguards and acceptance thresholds in NFR-3.4, and link high-risk outputs to the clinical review in NFR-8.6.
Define hallucination and accuracy metrics, validate against them, and document the results and known limitations in the instructions for use.

requirement_text: The app shall provide clear emergency instructions when urgent symptoms are detected.

assessment.summary: The supplied provisions (scientific panel alerts, notifying authorities, notified bodies, GPAI notifications, serious incident reporting timelines) do not impose a requirement-level obligation on an emergency-instruction display requirement. The listed serious-incident reporting provisions are system-level processes, not obligations for this UI behaviour.

requirement_text: The app shall log AI-generated advice for auditing and safety review.

assessment.summary: NFR-3.6 logs AI advice but does not define which events, metadata, or retention are recorded, so the logs may not support traceability, post-market monitoring, or the minimum six-month retention for a high-risk system.

risks.description: The requirement logs only 'AI-generated advice' and does not define the events needed for traceability (inputs, model/version, urgency classification, user overrides or challenges, errors, safety escalations), so risk situations and post-market monitoring cannot be supported.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for:
risks.engineering_action: Define a log event schema covering input context, model/version, output, urgency class, user feedback, challenge or dismissal, clinician review, and safety escalations. Map each field to Art. 12(2)(a)-(c).

addressed_by.covers: keeps records needed for clinical safety audits (partial support for 12(2)(a))

risks.description: No log retention period is set; the retention policy in NFR-13.5 is not tied to the AI logs and could delete them before the minimum six months, or conflict with that minimum.
risks.quote: the logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
risks.engineering_action: Specify a retention period for AI advice logs of at least six months, justified against the intended purpose and data protection law, and exempt these logs from ad hoc deletion. Add tamper-evident storage and an export path for authorities on request.

risks.description: Logs are stated to serve auditing and safety review but are not linked to post-market monitoring, so they may not be systematically collected and analysed for continuous compliance evaluation.
risks.quote: actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data
risks.engineering_action: State that AI advice logs feed a documented post-market monitoring process, with periodic analysis of unsafe-advice reports (FR-14.2), bias reviews (NFR-12.7), and incident triggers.

addressed_by.covers: collects user reports of incorrect or unsafe AI advice as monitoring input

recommendations: Define a log event schema covering inputs, model version, output, urgency class, overrides, reviews, and escalations, mapped to Art. 12(2).
Set a retention period of at least six months for AI advice logs, with tamper protection and authority access.
Link AI advice logs to a documented post-market monitoring process.

requirement_text: The app shall obtain user consent before collecting, storing, or sharing health information.

assessment.summary: NFR-4.2 is a data-protection consent control for health data, and the AI Act provisions supplied do not impose a requirement-level gap on it. The informed-consent provisions (Arts 60-61) apply only to real-world testing outside sandboxes, and Art 2(7) leaves personal-data consent to GDPR.

requirement_text: The app shall allow users to view, edit, export, or delete their personal data.

assessment.summary: NFR-4.3 gives users data-subject controls (view, edit, export, delete). These are GDPR-style rights, and the supplied AI Act provisions impose no requirement-level obligation on this function. Art. 2(7) confirms data protection law applies separately and the AI Act does not alter it.

requirement_text: The app shall anonymise or de-identify data where used for analytics or model improvement.

assessment.summary: NFR-4.6 is a privacy control for analytics and model-improvement data. It is not a gap in itself, but it does not tie model-improvement data to the data governance practices (origin, preparation, bias examination) that Article 10 requires for training, validation and testing data.

risks.description: The requirement does not say that de-identified data reused for model improvement (training, validation, testing) is subject to documented data-preparation, provenance and bias-examination practices, and it ignores the representativeness and quality loss that de-identification can cause.
risks.quote: relevant data-preparation processing operations, such as annotation, labelling, cleaning, updating, enrichment and aggregation;
risks.engineering_action: Define the de-identification method as a documented data-preparation step in the model-improvement pipeline. Record data origin and original collection purpose. Check that de-identification does not distort representativeness or hide bias-relevant attributes for older-adult subgroups.

addressed_by.covers: processes for reviewing bias in AI recommendations (partly 10(2)(f))

risks.description: The requirement does not handle the case where bias detection needs special-category data (health conditions, gender, age). It sets no rule that such data may be used only when anonymised or synthetic data is insufficient, nor safeguards such as access control, no onward transfer, and deletion after use.
risks.quote: the bias detection and correction cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data, including synthetic or anonymised data;
risks.engineering_action: Add an exception rule for bias testing. Anonymised or synthetic data is the default. Any use of special-category data requires documented necessity, restricted access, no transfer to third parties, and deletion once the bias is corrected.

addressed_by.covers: role-based access restriction for sensitive data
data retention and deletion policies

recommendations: Treat de-identification as a documented data-preparation step in the model-improvement pipeline, with provenance recording and a check that it preserves representativeness and bias-examination capability.

Add a rule that anonymised or synthetic data is the default for bias testing, and that any use of special-category data needs documented necessity, restricted access, no transfer, and deletion after use.

requirement_text: The app shall support secure authentication, such as passwords, PINs, biometrics, or multi-factor authentication.

assessment.summary: NFR-5.2 is a generic app-login control. The supplied provisions concern real-time/post remote biometric identification, which is not what user authentication is. The only mention of biometrics is optional device login, which is biometric verification (Art 3(36)), not identification. No requirement-level gap is supported by the supplied provisions.

requirement_text: The app shall maintain audit logs for access to sensitive information.

assessment.summary: NFR-5.5 covers access audit logs for sensitive information (a security/privacy control), but does not specify Article 12 event logging of AI system operation or a retention period. Other requirements partly cover AI-output logging, but the six-month minimum retention is not specified anywhere.

risks.description: The audit-log requirement is limited to access to sensitive information and sets no retention period, so the logs may not be kept for the minimum of six months required for logs of a high-risk AI system.
risks.quote: the logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
risks.engineering_action: Add a log retention requirement of at least six months, longer where clinical safety audits need it. Reconcile it with data-protection deletion rules (NFR-13.5) and document the justification.

risks.description: The requirement logs only data-access events and does not cover events relevant to AI risk identification, post-market monitoring or deployer monitoring, such as model version, inputs, outputs, overrides and urgency-classification changes. NFR-3.6 logs AI advice but not these other events.
risks.quote: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for: (a) identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk
risks.engineering_action: Define a log event schema for the AI components (symptom triage, assistant, emergency detection). It should capture model version, output, user override or dismissal, and safety-relevant anomalies, and it should be linked to the access-audit logs.

addressed_by.covers: automatic recording of AI-generated advice for auditing and safety review (12(1), partial 12(2))
activity log of caregiver actions (traceability of human actions)

recommendations: Specify a log retention period of at least six months for audit logs, aligned with the data deletion policy.
Extend logging to a defined set of AI operational events that supports risk identification and post-market monitoring, and cross-reference it with NFR-3.6.

requirement_text: The app shall use role-based access control for older adults, caregivers, clinicians, and administrators.

assessment.summary: NFR-5.6 sets role-based access control, which is a security and privacy control. None of the supplied provisions impose an obligation on RBAC for this requirement. The listed provisions concern EU database access, sandboxes, authority access and similar topics, and none creates a requirement-level gap.

requirement_text: The app shall prevent data loss during crashes or connectivity interruptions.

assessment.summary: NFR-6.4 states a data-loss prevention goal but does not say which data, what recovery objectives apply, or that crash and connectivity-failure events are recorded. Only Art. 15(4) resilience applies directly. Art. 12 logging is covered in part by other requirements, and the remaining gap is about preserving log and event integrity during failures.

risks.description: The requirement is vague about what must be protected and how (no scope, redundancy or fail-safe mechanism, no recovery targets). It does not say that AI-relevant data such as symptom urgency classifications, AI advice logs and audit logs is covered.
risks.quote: The robustness of high-risk AI systems may be achieved through technical redundancy solutions, which may include backup or fail-safe plans.
risks.engineering_action: Define the data classes covered (health inputs, medication confirmations, AI outputs, logs). Specify mechanisms such as local write-ahead persistence, sync with retry and conflict resolution, and idempotent writes. Set measurable targets (e.g. zero acknowledged-write loss, RPO/RTO) and test them with crash and network-fault injection.

addressed_by.covers: regular backups of user data, a backup solution under 15(4)
disaster recovery procedures as a fail-safe plan
graceful recovery from system errors
offline access to essential information

risks.description: The requirement does not guarantee that automatically generated logs (AI advice, caregiver actions, access events) and the crash and connectivity events themselves are durably recorded and not lost when the system fails, which would undermine traceability.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.
risks.engineering_action: State that log and audit records are persisted durably, with buffering and replay on reconnect and tamper-evident storage. Record crash and connectivity-interruption events as loggable events for post-market monitoring.

addressed_by.covers: logging of AI-generated advice for auditing
audit logs for access to sensitive information
records for clinical safety audits

recommendations: Rewrite NFR-6.4 to name the data classes covered, the persistence and sync mechanisms, and measurable data-loss targets, and verify them with fault-injection tests.
Add an explicit requirement that logs and audit trails survive crashes and offline periods, and that failures are themselves logged.

requirement_text: The app shall respond quickly to user interactions.

assessment.summary: NFR-7.2 is a general UI responsiveness requirement. It has no AI-specific function, and none of the supplied provisions (GPAI procedures, notified bodies, prohibited practices, transparency for AI interaction) impose a requirement-level obligation on it.

requirement_text: The AI assistant shall provide responses within an acceptable timeframe.

assessment.summary: NFR-7.3 is a non-functional response-time requirement with no measurable threshold. None of the supplied provisions (mostly GPAI, AI Office and notified-body procedures) impose a requirement-level obligation on response latency, so no compliance gap is supported.

requirement_text: The app shall support offline access to essential information such as medication schedules and emergency contacts.

assessment.summary: NFR-7.6 is an offline-availability requirement for non-AI data (medication schedules and emergency contacts). None of the supplied provisions imposes an obligation on it, so no requirement-level compliance gap is identified.

requirement_text: The app shall regularly update its medical knowledge base.

assessment.summary: NFR-8.5 requires regular knowledge-base updates but none of the supplied provisions imposes an obligation that this requirement fails to meet. The provisions concern notified bodies, Commission procedures, and general documentation and logging, not knowledge-base maintenance.

requirement_text: The system shall support regular software updates and bug fixes.

assessment.summary: NFR-9.3 only says the system supports updates and bug fixes. It has no change-control step to decide whether an update is a substantial modification that triggers a new conformity assessment under Article 43(4). Without one, a high-risk health AI system could be changed in ways that alter compliance without re-assessment.

risks.description: Updates and bug fixes have no change-classification or release-gating step to decide whether a change is a substantial modification (affecting compliance or intended purpose) that requires a new conformity assessment, or whether it was pre-determined in the technical documentation.
risks.quote: High-risk AI systems that have already been subject to a conformity assessment procedure shall undergo a new conformity assessment procedure in the event of a substantial modification
risks.engineering_action: Reword NFR-9.3 to require a documented change-control process. Each update would be assessed against the Article 3(23) substantial-modification criteria. Pre-determined changes would be recorded in the technical documentation. Substantial modifications would be blocked from release until re-assessment is complete. Each decision and its rationale would be recorded.

recommendations: Add a change-control and release-gating procedure to NFR-9.3 that classifies each update as substantial or non-substantial under Article 3(23), keeps the technical documentation current, and triggers a new conformity assessment where required.
